subject: Clarify operator demarcation, BYOK, and cross-border access for Private Deployment
messages:
From: Samira Khan <samira.khan@orchidhealth.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@orchidhealth.com
Date: Fri, 30 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify operator demarcation, BYOK, and cross-border access for Private Deployment

Hi Jonas / Karthik,

Thanks for the demo last week. We're evaluating Redwood for a VPC/private deployment for our clinical data pipelines and have a handful of follow-ups from legal/security and procurement. High-level asks below — can you confirm behavior and whether we can get formal language for our DPA addendum?

1) BYOK: we plan to hold customer-managed CMKs in our KMS. We need a clear statement that Redwood operators cannot access unencrypted customer data or KEKs. Is there any breakglass process where Redwood personnel can decrypt or access CMKs? If so, please describe controls (audit trail, approvals, time-limited).

2) Operator telemetry & limited visibility: we need confirmation of the exact telemetry Redwood collects from private deployments (agent heartbeats, instance metadata, service logs). Anything that might contain customer identifiers needs to be enumerated.

3) Cross-border replication & support: if we enable regional failover, will customer data or keys leave the US without explicit consent? For regulatory reasons, we may want a hard restriction to US-only storage for this account.

4) Evidence pack: SOC 2 report, sample audit logs showing operator access events, and a short ops-access matrix mapping roles to capabilities.

Could you respond with proposed contract language (short clauses) we can add to the DPA and attach the ops access matrix? Procurement would also like a timeline for finalizing the addendum and signing.

Thanks — Samira
Samira Khan
Head of Security, Orchid Health
From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <samira.khan@orchidhealth.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, irene_choi@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 30 Mar 2028 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify operator demarcation, BYOK, and cross-border access for Private Deployment

Samira — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front, then attachments and next steps.

1) BYOK / operator access: Redwood supports customer-managed keys. Operators do not have the ability to directly retrieve customer CMKs or plaintext model inputs/outputs. Breakglass: we do have a documented emergency access procedure for on-premair-gapped and VPC setups that requires (a) two-person on-call approval, (b) an automated ticket created in the customer's ticketing webhook and ours, and (c) HSM-controlled split access. Any breakglass event is time-limited (max 4 hours) and must be recorded with artifacts (session recording + signed approval). Suggested DPA clause in attachment A.

2) Telemetry & visibility: by default, our agent emits health heartbeats, GPU/CPU counters, and anonymized error codes. We do not transmit customer payloads. I've attached an ops-access matrix (ops-access-matrix.xlsx) showing exactly which telemetry fields are sent. If Orchid wants to remove a field, we can gate it behind a config flag for private deployments.

3) Regional replication: we can configure private replication to be US-only. We will add explicit contract language that no cross-border replication will occur without written consent from Orchid.

4) Evidence pack: we will provide SOC 2 Type II summary (redacted), a sample audit log extract, and a draft DPA addendum.

Attachments: redwood-byok-boundary-proposal.pdf (proposal language + operator demarcation), ops-access-matrix.xlsx (telemetry fields)

Next steps: I'll loop in Irene to finalize the DPA clause language and Karthik for legal ops alignment. Can we target a call next week to walk procurement through the clause and signoff?

— Jonas
Jonas Weber
Principal Product Manager, Security & Privacy
Redwood Inference
From: irene_choi@redwood.ai <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 01 Apr 2028 10:22:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Clarify operator demarcation, BYOK, and cross-border access for Private Deployment

Jonas / team — quick internal notes to tighten the language before we send the DPA addendum draft to Orchid: 

- Make breakglass non-bypassable: require both customer OOO keyholder + Redwood Director approval (two distinct orgs).
- Limit forensic access scope in the clause: explicitly list allowed artefacts (logs, memory snapshot hashes) and prohibit key export.
- Add a clause prohibiting operator telemetry from including any PII or PHI; if any telemetry could contain identifiers, it must be filtered/hashed client-side by default.
- Add a 30-day notice period for any change in subprocessor list and a right-to-audit for critical subprocessors handling control plane telemetry.

I'm attaching a short DPA addendum template (dpa-addendum-draft.docx) with suggested redlines. Karthik — can you review the wording on subprocessor notice and the audit right? I can then combine and send to Samira with a proposed call time.

— Irene
Irene Choi
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference
From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <samira.khan@orchidhealth.com>, procurement@orchidhealth.com
Cc: irene_choi@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 03 Apr 2028 15:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify operator demarcation, BYOK, and cross-border access for Private Deployment

Samira — attaching the DPA addendum draft and a short summary of the evidence pack. Quick bullet plan so procurement has clarity: 

- We attach the DPA addendum (dpa-addendum-draft.docx) which includes: BYOK clause (no-key-export, two-org breakglass), telemetry prohibition on PII/PHI, and subprocessor notice + 30-day window.
- Evidence pack we will share within 48 hours after you confirm NDA scope: SOC 2 Type II summary (redacted), sample audit log (operator-event-sample.csv), and the ops-access-matrix.xlsx that lists telemetry fields.
- Proposed legal timeline: sign DPA addendum in DocuSign within 10 business days after final redlines.
- Proposed meeting: Thu 2028-04-06 11:00 PT — 30m — to run through the addendum and procurement checklist. Please confirm or suggest an alternate time.

DocuSign link (placeholder): https://www.docusign.com/some/placeholder/12345

Attachments referenced: dpa-addendum-draft.docx, ops-access-matrix.xlsx, redwood-byok-boundary-proposal.pdf

Thanks — looking forward to wrapping this up.

— Jonas
